title: Review of Speak Mandarin Campaign and Stance on Chinese Dialects
what_it_is: Review of Speak Mandarin Campaign and Stance on Chinese Dialects

sections.label: Speak Mandarin Campaign launch
sections.summary: The Speak Mandarin Campaign, launched in 1979, promotes Mandarin as a common language across dialect backgrounds and supports the bilingual policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: The Speak Mandarin Campaign was launched in 1979.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: By promoting a common language across the Chinese community, it helps Chinese Singaporeans from different dialect backgrounds to communicate with one another and it preserves access to the Chinese culture through Mandarin, rather than through separate dialects.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: By simplifying the linguistic environment, it also gives our bilingual policy the best chance to succeed.

sections.label: Campaign evolves to cultural identity
sections.summary: The campaign has evolved to strengthen Singapore Chinese cultural identity and make Mandarin learning fun, with more curriculum time in education.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: Singapore families are using English more at home and much as our young want to be better at Mandarin, the opportunities to do so may be insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: So, hence the campaign has evolved from promoting Mandarin as a common language, to strengthening their appreciation for our Singapore Chinese cultural identity and making the learning of Mandarin fun and enjoyable.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: In education, the Ministry of Social and Family Development and the Ministry of Education are setting aside more curriculum time to expose young Chinese students to Mandarin.

sections.label: Dialect use decline and heritage
sections.summary: As English displaces mother tongues, dialect use declines, and dialect artistic materials are seen as heritage that deepens cultural appreciation.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: As the use of English continues to displace mother tongues, the use of dialects in Singapore, has continued to decline.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: We increasingly see dialect artistic materials, not as competing against the use of Mandarin, but as part of our heritage and cultural practices that deepen Singaporeans' appreciation of our cultural heritage.

sections.label: Government welcomes dialect preservation ideas
sections.summary: The Government welcomes ideas to preserve dialect cultures while upholding the importance of Mandarin.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: The Government welcomes ideas to preserve dialect cultures while upholding the importance of Mandarin.
